01 WHO IS AUDEMARS 
PIGUET? 
 
Audemars Piguet is a Swiss fine watchmaking house, based in Le Brassus, which was founded 
in Vallé de Joux in 1875 by Jules Louis Audemars and Edward Auguste Piguet under the name 
“Audemars Piguet & Cie”, completes together with Patek Philippe and Vacheron Constantin the 
“Holy Trinity” from Swiss watchmaking. 
 
These two men were watchmakers, Audemars created several extremely 
complexes for brands such as “Tiffany&Co” while Piguet specialized in regulating 
movements. 
When the brand began its activity, responsibility was divided in such a way as to entrust 
Audemars handled production and technical development while Piguet handled management and sales. 
Since its foundation, this brand has been in the “hands” of the same families (The Audemars family 
and the Piguet Family). 
 
Audemars Piguet (AP) has been a major influence on luxury watchmaking since its inception. 
its founding in 1875 and continues to shape the industry with constant innovation both in terms 
design and in technical terms. The brand has contributed significantly to shaping the 
luxury watch industry with some notable innovations. 
 
They are: 
➢ 1892: Created the first minute repeating movement for wristwatches, which 
it was later sold to Louis Brandt frères (Omega SA). 
 
➢ 1899: Manufactured a "Grand Complication" pocket watch with seven complications, 
including “grand strike” and “small strike”, minute repeater”, alarm, “perpetual calendar”, 
“deadbeat seconds”, “chronoograph with jumping seconds” and a “split seconds hand”. 
 
➢ 1921: Created the first “jumping-hour” wristwatch, powered by the Caliber 
HPVM10.
AudemarsPiguet.txt_page_5:
5 
 
➢ 1934: Introduced the first “skeleton” watch. 
 
➢ 1946: Produced the thinnest watch, with a 1.64 mm thick movement. 
 
➢ 1972: Introduced the first “sportswatch” wristwatch, the “Royal Oak”. 
 
➢ 1986: Created the ultra-thin automatic watch with tourbillon (Caliber 2870), measuring just 5.3 
mm thick (including case). 
 
➢ 1995/96: Manufactured the first automatic watch "Grand Complication" (Caliber 2885). 
 
➢ 2006: Introduced the first direct impulse exhaust, based on a design from the 
watchmaker Robert Robin, from the 18th century. 
 
➢ 2007/08: Developed the first watch with a carbon case and carbon movement 
(Royal Oak Carbon Concept). 
 
➢ 2015: Launched the first mechanical chronograph with independent memory and three wheels 
column, called “Royal Oak Concept Laptimer Michael Schumacher”. 
 
➢ 2019: Introduced the world's thinnest automatic perpetual calendar.

aesthetics and watchmaking for the 21st century. With complex geometry box

03 MARKETING MIX 
 
AUDEMARS PIGUET 
 
Product: Strongly bets on boldness and innovation. The Royal Oak line is its icon 
Absolute, mixing industrial design with artisanal finishing. Launches limited pieces, uses 
materials such as ceramics, forged carbon, and focus on proprietary movements. Likes to tease 
with unexpected designs and cultural “collabs”. 
 
Price: Positioned in the “ultra-luxury” segment, but with a more “culturally 
desired” than just traditional. Entrance prices are around 20–25 thousand euros, 
but exclusive pieces can exceed 200 thousand. The perceived value is high, in part due to 
“hype” and scarcity. 
 
Place: Has invested in an almost exclusively direct distribution model, through 
its “AP Houses” in key cities. It left many multi-brand retailers to control 
better experience and positioning. Some editions are accessible only by invitation or 
relationship with the brand. 
 
Promotion: Communicates in a modern way, with a strong digital presence. Collaborate with 
artists, musicians, athletes and participates in events such as “Art Basel”. The brand bets on 
impactful visual narratives, behind-the-scenes content, and videos that associate the watch with 
contemporary culture and performance. 
 
PATEK PHILLIPE 
 
Product: It is the guardian of tradition. Their watches are classic, conservative in design and 
highly sophisticated in movements. Invests a lot in Grand Complications and calibers 
own. Each piece is made to last for generations, without giving in to fashions. The focus is on inheritance and 
technical perfection. 
 
Price: Operates with an even higher pricing strategy, based on the idea of legacy and 
investment. A Calatrava starts at 25 thousand euros, but complications and special editions 
they easily rise to 500 thousand or more. It's a mark of heritage, not ostentation.
AudemarsPiguet.txt_page_14:
14 
Place: Remains faithful to the traditional distribution model: authorized points of sale 
highly selective and few own boutiques. The purchase is often shrouded in 
formality and restricted access, reinforcing the idea of prestige and scarcity. 
 
Promotion: Maintains a reserved and institutional tone. Its most famous campaign, “You 
never actually own a Patek Philippe...”, focuses on generational value. The brand avoids celebrities, 
remains discreet on social media and favors word-of-mouth among collectors. 
 
VACHERON CONSTANTIN 
 
Product: Focuses on artistic “savoir-faire”. The brand favors manual finishing, 
enamels, engravings and other traditional watchmaking arts. Pieces such as the “Métiers d’Art” and “Les 
Cabinotiers” reinforce the status of mechanical jewelry. It has a more poetic and artistic touch, 
without giving up the technique. 
 
Price: Prices are in line with haute horlogerie, although slightly below the PP in 
“entry-level”. A Patrimony can start at around 18 thousand euros. At the top, the pieces “Les 
Cabinotiers” easily exceed 300 thousand. The value is in art and tradition, more than 
in immediate social status. 
 
Place: Opts for a hybrid model: maintains presence in luxury retailers and boutiques 
own, with increasing investment in brand experience and digital. It also offers 
sales to order and service by appointment for demanding customers. 
 
Promotion: Communicates through art and detail. “Storytelling” is centered on 
heritage, technical precision and manual arts. The brand participates in events 
cultural and watchmaking (such as “Watches & Wonders”) and invests in videos with a tone 
inspiring and calm, unhurried, like your watches.

05 “GOLDEN CIRCLE” 
The “Golden Circle” exists as a “framework” used to define how a 
brand communicates.  
It establishes that communication must be done from the inside out, starting with “passing” 
purposes and values before promoting products or services. 
This “framework then allows effectiveness in strengthening the emotional relationship between the public and 
visa brand makes it communicate in a way that is “perceived” as more human and 
genuine. 
Since Audemars Piquet sells luxury watches that no one “needs” is important 
add the greatest possible value to the brand (“perceived” or not). 
 
The AP “Golden Circle” exists in the following form: 
 
WHY – (The Reason for Being) 
Create magnificent and complex pieces of time that transcend functionality, where each 
it is an artistic expression of mastery, heritage and innovation. 
This is the heart of the brand: passion, legacy and creative boldness. It's not just about watches, 
it is a legacy that is worn on the wrist. 
 
HOW – (The Single Process) 
Preserving the “savoir-faire” of Swiss watchmaking through artisanal processes led by 
master watchmakers who fuse tradition with innovation.

This creation method highlights rarity, exclusivity, authenticity and a human touch, 
exactly what the contemporary luxury consumer values most. 
 
WHAT – (The Offer) 
Swiss watches of exceptional complexity that combine traditional watchmaking techniques with 
cutting-edge innovation, each piece is a limited edition work of art. 
From Royal Oak to Code 11.59, AP's offering is never just a product, it's a statement 
cultural.

Theoretical Framework 
The theoretical foundation of this report is based on the evolution of paradigms of 
digital communication, exploring the concepts that support communication methodologies 
capture, conversion and automation applied during the internship. 
1. The Evolution of Marketing: From Institutional to Marketing 5.0 
The Higher Education ecosystem has historically operated under a logic of 
institutional and passive reputation marketing, strongly anchored in tactics 
Top of Funnel (TOFU) generalists. However, the consumer journey 
Contemporary demands a more sophisticated approach. According to Kotler, Kartajaya and 
Setiawan (2021), the transition to "Marketing 5.0" dictates the application of technologies 
that mimic human behavior to create, communicate and deliver value. 
Today, the enrollment decision of a potential student is not dictated solely by 
static prestige of the institution, but due to the technical capacity of the brand in 
intercept your search intent in an agile and personalized way (Kotler et al., 
2021). This evolution underlies the urgency of transitioning from a reactive operation 
for a data-driven infrastructure. 
2. Performance Marketing and SEO: Visibility and Conversion 
In the field of Digital Marketing, effectiveness is measured by the ability to generate 
tangible results through the strategic management of digital channels. Chaffey and 
Ellis-Chadwick (2019) emphasize that the success of the online presence depends on the 
optimizing the intersection between user intent and brand offering, 
transforming the digital ecosystem into a surgical conversion engine. No 
context of search engines, this approach requires an exhaustive search of 
keywords and continuous monitoring, applied both to 
paid advertising (Search Engine Marketing - SEM) and organic traffic (Search

Engine Optimization - SEO). Ryan (2016) reinforces that the alignment between the 
investment in ads and organic authority guarantees that the institution does not 
acquires only volume of traffic, but qualified relevance, maximizing the 
Return on Investment (ROI). 
3. Data Analytics and Integration: From Noise to Actionable Decision 
In the context of digital analytics, the true usefulness of data does not lie in its 
mere accumulation, but in the ability to extract actionable insights. Kaushik (2010) 
argues that organizations must move away from obsessing over performance metrics 
vanity and focusing on data that drives business decisions. This premise 
theory supports the development of integrated analytical infrastructures 
(crossing tools such as Google Ads and Google Search Console). When processing 
these metrics centrally, technical SEO and campaign management 
cease to be empirical tasks and become strictly 
driven by real performance data, allowing route corrections in time 
useful. 
4. Direct Communication and Loyalty: Permission Marketing 
Lead capture and subsequent email communication should 
move away from intrusive logic. The concept of "Permission Marketing", coined 
by Godin (1999), is based on the privilege of sending advance messages, 
personal and relevant to individuals who have expressed a voluntary desire for the 
receive. This theory underlies the need to design forms of 
optimized capture that reduces friction in the user journey and allows 
primary segmentation. By applying segmentation right at the moment of conversion, 
institution ensures that direct communication via email marketing is highly 
relevant, which, according to Chaffey and Ellis-Chadwick (2019), increases 
significantly increase open rates and conversion likelihood over the course of 
digital funnel.

Artificial Intelligence (AI). The integration of AI agents and language models

The Brand Key Framework is a structure that helps brands 
be able to define their strategy, tone of voice, among other aspects (Appendix, image 1).

The essential strength, which consists of the identity and essence of the brand.  
The competitive environment, which is the analysis of competition in the market where the brand 
is found. 
The ideal target audience, which are the people we want to reach. 
The benefits for the consumer, which is where the brand shows the customer why

24 years ago, on September 30th, I was backstage at the Paris Auto Show, waiting 
for the CC8S to be wheeled out to the crowd, eager to see everyone’s reaction to this creation 
that me and the team worked so hard to unveil. 
At that moment, I didn't think about the possibilities and what could be; I simply 
wanted people to see it, wanted people to get excited for this machine and this dream that 
began as a couple of rough sketches done in my parent’s bedroom. 
No thoughts of the CCR, the Agera, or the Jesko, no thoughts of Freevalve or DDT, 
nor any other models and technologies our company has produced over the years. A few 
people have come and gone, some teams changed, some expanded, and some became their 
own thing, like Freevalve. 
Eight models were released since that pleasant September day: 
1. 2002 – Koenigsegg CC8S 
2. 2004 – Koenigsegg CCR 
3. 2006 – Koenigsegg CCX 
4. 2011 – Koenigsegg Agera 
5. 2015 – Koenigsegg Agera RS 
6. 2016 – Koenigsegg Regera 
7. 2021 – Koenigsegg Jesko 
8. 2022 – Koenigsegg Gemera 
9. 2023 – Koenigsegg CC850 
And what a ride it has been, with every following release. Koenigsegg has continued 
to push the envelope when it comes to performance and driving experience, always looking 
to improve on what’s been done. 
We have seen many competitors come and go, others keep pushing and being pushed 
by, never letting them rest on their laurels and hoping they do the same for us. 
And that brings us to today. I’m not one much for sentimentalism, but even I know 
the importance of a 25-year anniversary, a quarter century of car manufacturing and 
automobile development that started as an idea in the mind of a young Swedish boy. 
We don’t plan to let a date of such importance go by without recognizing it, and 
certainly not without something worthy of such a date. And so, with that idea in mind, 
Koenigsegg will be present at the 2025 Paris Auto Show, on September 30th, at the exact 
same spot and show where it all started for young Christian von Koenigsegg. 
Thank you for taking this journey with us and “KVARTSSEKELsjubileum.” 
Christian Von Koenigsegg 
CEO, Koenigsegg

2.6.2.4 Email Marketing 
Visual representation in image group 24 of the annex. 
Our goal with email marketing is to establish an automated response 
which will reach those who provide us with their email on the landing page created especially for 
the event. 
They only contain a reference to the event and its date and three CTAs, one to watch 
to the “live stream”, one to purchase tickets and another to add the date to your calendar. 
A simple email with little information, and images that reference the 
anniversary of the launch, quick to read and “digest”. 
2.6.2.5 Website + Landing Page 
Visual representation in group of images 25 of the annex (Link also present). 
The landing page was designed with a simple and direct design, containing only the 
brand logo and a form for collecting essential data: email, name, age, gender 
and occupation. 
Submitting this form triggers the automatic sending of an email to the 
user, containing more information about the event. This email also includes several 
Strategic CTAs, namely: direct access to the launch livestream, possibility 
to purchase tickets and an option to add the date to the user's personal calendar. 
At this point, there is no audience segmentation. This component will be 
introduced at a later stage, after the initial data collection, allowing a 
more personalized and effective communication.

WHAT IS NERF?
"Inverse Rendering" technology that uses
Artificial Intelligence to transform 2D photos and videos
into photorealistic, volumetric 3D experiences.
NERF
NeRF_Photogrammetry.txt_page_3:
Home
About
Contact
 Volume vs. Surface
Ray Marching
The Neural Function
NeRF does not create solid surfaces. He “sees” space
as a volume of density (like fog). This
allows you to represent glass, smoke and reflections, as
calculates what is in and through the object, not just
the shell.
To create the final image, the computer shoots "rays"
of virtual light through this volume. The ray passes through the
object, accumulating color and density along the way
to form the final pixel on the screen.
Instead of storing geometry, NeRF stores a function
mathematics. Receives coordinates (XYZ + Direction of
Gaze) and the generative model returns the color and density
at that exact point. It is a "Color Coordinate".

FUNDAMENTALS

Capturing Light (View
Dependency):
In classical theory, the color of an object is static
(ink).
In NeRF, the color is Dynamic (View Dependent). The AI
learn that the color of a point changes depending
from where the observer is. (This is the theoretical basis
to achieve photorealism in metals and glass.)
From "Explicit" to
"Implicit":
Before (Photogrammetry): 3D was based on
Explicit Geometry (triangles and meshes). O
computer needed to know exactly where
the surface began and ended. Failed to
smooth or transparent surfaces.
Now (NeRF): 3D becomes Representation
Implicit. The object is not saved as a
form, but rather as a "memory" in the network
neural. The form "appears" only when
we asked the AI.

The Process:
Capture: Take a series of photographs (20 to 100+) around the object,
ensuring that each photo overlaps the previous one.
Upload: Upload the original images (preferably in high resolution)
directly to the cloud software.
Automatic Processing:
The software calculates the position of the cameras.
If it is NeRF: Train the neural network.
If Splatting: Generates and optimizes the point cloud.
Export: 
Creation of an interactive web file (HTML/WebGL) or video.

Reduction in Returns:
NeRF eliminates surprise. By capturing the texture and
real imperfections (photorealism), the client knows
exactly what you are buying.
Data: Fewer returns in e-commerce mean
direct profit margin protection.
The Death of the Product Photo:
We are seeing the end of static photography
product. Consumer expectations are shifting towards
“Try before you buy” digitally.
Attention Economy and UX:
The modern consumer ignores static photos ("banner
blindness"). An interactive object creates active engagement
(touch, rotation), increasing the time spent in the
website (Dwell Time) and SEO.
Concept: "Gamification without games".
COPE Strategy:
"Create Once, Publish Everywhere". A single NeRF scan
generates: the 3D viewer for the website, the AR filter for Instagram and
the VFX assets for the TV ad.

01 INTRODUCTION 
 
This work aims to carry out an analysis that seeks to compare the 
online presence (in the field of online advertising with an exclusive focus on Google 
Search Ads) from two direct competitors of the chosen brand (OMEGA) for the project 
final, which in this case are: Rolex and Grand Seiko. 
These brands have markedly different positions with regards to the Ethos of 
watchmaking that they design, produce and sell, Ethos esse, which is also 
manifests itself in the way they build their Ads, from Headlines to Descriptions. 
For analysis purposes, a Paid Search Ad was chosen from each of these 
companies that were online on 3/11/2025. 
 
02 CONTEXTUALIZATION 
OF THE SECTOR  
 
The luxury watchmaking sector operates at a unique intersection of engineering, art and 
psychology. Essentially, these brands do not sell the function of measuring time, 
but rather aspiration, a tangible symbol of success, heritage and status. This reality 
dictates that marketing is mainly based on building desire and 
trust, which explains the inversion of the traditional funnel: TOFU (Awareness) is 
typically built through expensive and emotional offline channels (sponsorships, 
elite events), while MOFU and BOFU (Consideration and Action) are managed with 
surgical precision in digital. The accelerated transition to e-commerce, amplified 
due to recent events, has forced brands like Rolex to defend their image with 
even more rigor, and growing brands like Grand Seiko using digital 
scientific and aggressive way to convert high purchase intention into sales 
immediate.
ROLEXVSGRANDSEIKO.txt_page_4:
4 
03 DESCRIPTION OF 
BRANDS (ROLEX AND GRAND 
SEIKO) 
 
The Rolex brand positions itself as the global icon of luxury watchmaking, with a strong 
emphasis on robustness, accuracy and universal recognition. Founded in 1905 in 
London by Hans Wilsdorf, a German, and later transferred to Geneva, the 
Rolex pioneered numerous technical innovations, including creating the first 
water-resistant case (Oyster) and automatic movement with Perpetual rotor. This 
history of innovation and reliability has consolidated its prestigious reputation and 
durability. The brand's Ethos is based on this tradition, characteristics that are 
clearly reflect in the way you communicate through your Marketing. 
 
 
Figure 1-Print Ad Rolex
ROLEXVSGRANDSEIKO.txt_page_5:

In turn, Grand Seiko presents a more discreet and 
contemplative, focused on artisanal perfection and subtle technical innovation. Founded 
in 1960 by Seiko, Grand Seiko emerged with the aim of penetrating the 
luxury by creating watches that rival the best in Switzerland (still 
thus its first presence outside Asia was in 2017), combining engineering 
precision with minimalist aesthetics and artisanal finishing, characteristics that are 
associated with this culture. The brand's Ethos emphasizes meticulous care for each 
detail, high precision and natural beauty of the design, which translates into 
Marketing that favors more poetic and technical messages. 
 
 
Figure 2-Print Ad Grand Seiko

05 FUNNEL PHASE 
 
In the world of luxury watchmaking (or any good of this kind) people who 
do not know or buy our product are as important as those that 
do, it is this reality that makes the appeal to aspirations so strong and effective, for this reason 
reason, most of the budget of these brands is spent creating this aspiration (Phase 
of Awareness) and outside the “GSA”, leaving Google Search for the 
Consideration and Action. 
 
While in the intricacies of traditional marketing a wider “net” is cast 
due to the fact that these means deal with the inherent difficulties of segmentation, 
in digital, this filtering can be performed without major difficulties. 
In the case of these two brands and, by extension, their competitors, the change of 
paradigm brought by COVID, dictated that the transition to a more 
dependent on digital happened sooner than perhaps they would have wanted. 
 
This funnel distinction is crucial: the content of Print Ads (TOFU), which builds the aura 
of exclusivity, is the aspirational promise that the GSA has to fulfill. Analyzing the 
press campaigns, it is clear that Rolex (through its 
explorer/conquest) carries its promise of timeless authority 
directly to digital, refusing the explicit transaction as in its 
press campaigns. Grand Seiko (with its focus on subtle art and nature) 
uses its artisanal reputation (the Ethos built offline) as the final argument of 
sale in GSA.  
What the customer sees in the magazine (the Aspiration) has to be validated by what the customer sees 
on Google (Execution). Online advertising thus becomes the functional extension of 
narrative established in traditional channels. 
 
The addition of the digital aspect to operations required brands to make the decision 
where this medium fit in, whether in a phase of awareness, consideration or action and 
This analysis will demonstrate that Rolex chose to use the “GSA” as a point of 
primary contact in the Consideration phase, MOFU, focusing on the Image 
Corporate. 
While Grand Seiko, focusing on market growth, integrated the GSA 
as a crucial channel of Action, BOFU, albeit with a secondary objective of 
bring some notoriety to the brand outside of Asia.

06 KEYWORDS 
 
Initially, keyword analysis is carried out using a strategy 
called “Trial and Error”, where several search terms were used that would 
sense to trigger the chosen ad. 
Next, Google Keyword Planner is used to try to understand that 
other search terms could trigger the ad. 
This point will be separated by brand. 
 
GRAND SEIKO: 
 
Keyword analysis shows that Grand Seiko prioritizes Conversion and Efficiency 
(BOFU) rather than broad visibility. Taking into account the objective of direct sales and the 
creating notoriety in the West, Grand Seiko uses a strategic mix of 
keywords MOFU and BOFU (the BOFU intention being preponderant). This approach 
aims to convert users who are in the decision phase, using information 
“MOFU” only when necessary to support the conversion perspective. 
 
Grand Seiko's absolute focus on Conversion (BOFU) implies a strong dependence 
of high-precision match types, such as [Exact Match] and “Phrase Match”. This choice 
minimizes spend on more diffuse intent (MOFU) search terms, ensuring 
that each click has the highest potential Return on Investment (ROI). 
 
 
Using “Trial and Error” it was possible to draw a good image of the 
Grand Seiko's strategy, the first search term that originally showed the ad was 
Grand Seiko which, given that it is the name of the brand, makes sense. 
 
Afterwards, with the notion that BOFU is a target, we move on to Search Terms with intentions

2.2.1.1 Saoloto's Purpose 
"We believe that it is possible to find peace in the midst of the rush." 
This purpose constitutes the core identity of Saoloto and reflects the commitment to 
transform surfing into an experience of balance and deep belonging. The brand 
assumes itself as the "Portuguese surfing house", a welcoming space that functions as 
a refuge of serenity in the face of the acceleration of urban daily life, but which is, above all, 
a meeting point of cultures. 
The foundation of this vision is the creation of an inclusive and global ecosystem, 
where Portuguese hospitality merges with Samoan heritage. By uniting individuals from all over 
the world, from the amateur looking for their first connection with the sea (like Kelly, or the 
Duarte) to the experienced surfer who seeks the technical and spiritual essence of the sport (as 
Lukas), Saoloto proves that the sea is a space for communion.

2.2.4.1 Storytelling and Message 
Saoloto's narrative is not a mere description of services, but a construction 
myth that gives a deep purpose to the consumer experience. Storytelling works 
as the common thread that connects Samoan ancestral heritage to the contemporary context of surfing 
in Portugal, allowing the public to see themselves on a journey of personal and 
collective. By adopting the motto “Where the Waves Sculpt Family”, the brand assumes the 
responsibility to tell a story that challenges the conventional and individualistic view of 
sport, proposing the following narrative arc: 
Saoloto: The Strength of the Tribe at Sea 
●​
Common World: Contemporary surfing has become a sport of 
isolation. Schools focus on individual performance, on the technique of "me" against the wave. 
The image is sold of the lonely, disconnected surfer, who sees the ocean only as a 
stage for your ego and personal achievement. It is unknown that, in Samoan origins, surfing 
it was never a solo act, but an extension of the tribe's life. 
●​
Problem: This purely technical and individualistic vision creates a rupture 
dangerous. When we separate the surfer from his environment and peers, we lose the essence 
spirituality of practice. We forget that treating the ocean as an object separates us from 
nature, and treating surfing as an isolated achievement separates us from humanity. Without the 
connection to the whole, the technique is empty and the surfer remains incomplete. 
●​
Solution: Saoloto Surf School recovers the ancestral perspective: we don't surf 
in the ocean, you surf with him and with others. Our pedagogy goes beyond maneuvering; 
we build an experience where the student learns to breathe in unison with the tide and the 
group. We teach that the wave does not belong to anyone, it is shared, just like the energy that 
moves us. 
●​
Transformation: We restore the lost link between man, the gods and the 
group. The big lesson is the Samoan paradox: only when someone truly becomes 
part of a community is that it can rise up as an individual. At Saoloto, you are no longer 
a solitary visitor at sea to become part of a living ecosystem, finding your 
identity through belonging.

2.3.4.2.3 Diagnosis - Problems and Optimizations 
This point aims to demonstrate the team’s critical capacity in 
anticipate and mitigate potential problems, demonstrating a strategic vision that goes beyond the 
idealized planning. Although the risk scenarios are varied, three were identified 
possibilities for which Saoloto Surf School presents answers in advance 
outlined. 
1st Problem: 
●​ AToP (Avg. Time on Page) very high on the "History" and "Legends" pages. 
●​ Very low CVR (Conversion Rate). 
Website visitors spend a fairly healthy amount of time on 
pages that contain authentic and genuine content about the history and legends of surfing, 
unfortunately the conversion rate remains very low.

Optimization: People are immersed in reading the Samoan spirit (which explains 
time on the page high), but the site works like a museum: the user reads, gets inspired, and goes 
although because the buy button disappeared up there. 
Implement a "Sticky CTA Button" that floats on top or 
bottom of the screen and follows the user's scroll. This ensures that the "Book 
Class" is always visible at the exact moment the user feels inspired by the 
story, without breaking the fluidity of reading. 
2nd Problem: 
●​ High CCR (Cultural Content Reach) and CGR (Community Growth). 
●​ Low BSV (Branded Search Volume) in the school's local area. 
In this situation, cultural content demonstrates solid performance. O 
its consumption and distribution contribute positively to the growth of the community. No 
However, this growth may occur mainly in international markets where the 
Demand for surfing is not particularly high. 
Even though Saoloto positions itself as an international school, 
(considering that the language of surfing is universal) there are markets where the demand for 
this practice is extremely limited. Thus, a community composed largely of 
percentage by individuals coming from these markets will hardly translate into 
conversions. 
Optimization: The social platforms algorithm is optimizing the distribution of 
content to where "taste" is cheaper and more abundant, ignoring the likelihood of 
actual purchase. The budget is paying for vanity metrics in markets that do not 
consume the product. Implement a "Negative Geo-Targeting" strategy (Exclusion 
Geographic) in top-of-funnel campaigns. 
Markets identified as bearish must be explicitly added 
propensity for cold water surfing to the list of excluded locations. This forces the algorithm to 
redistribute the budget to markets with compatible surf culture (such as Japan, USA or 
Northern Europe), exchanging volume of followers for quality of potential customers. 
3rd Problem: 
●​ High BSV (Branded Search Volume) (many people search for the brand). 
84
Saoloto_Campaign_Strategy.txt_page_86:
●​ CVR (Conversion Rate) drops specifically for beginners. 
●​ Neutral/confused BSS (Brand Sentiment) in the comments (“Is this just for pros?”). 
This scenario generally occurs in brands that rely heavily on history and 
surfing legends, which can lead the potential client, in this case the beginner, to perceive the 
brand as excessively cool or hardcore.  
Despite there being a high volume of searches associated with the brand, the rate of 
conversion of this segment is residual. Additionally, the dominant feeling is one of confusion, 
since it is not clear whether the school is aimed exclusively at experienced surfers or whether 
also welcomes beginners. This ambiguity, often reflected in the comments of 
publications, tends to alienate this more inexperienced audience. 
Optimizations: 
1st – The isolated interest in “Surf” or “Polynesian Culture” is excessively 
comprehensive for an international surf school. A user can identify with the 
Saoloto vibe without ever leaving its home country. In international markets, the 
Segmentation must therefore resort to Travel Intent Layering, crossing interest in “Surf” 
with mandatory behaviors such as “Frequent International Travelers” or “Interest 
in Travel to Portugal”. 
This approach allows us to filter out the so-called “couch fans” and ensure that the narrative 
of Samoan Legend is only delivered to users who, statistically, demonstrate 
propensity and financial capacity to travel to school. 
2nd – The iconography associated with “Warriors” and “Ancestral Legends” is creating a 
psychological barrier to entry, implicitly suggesting that error, failure or lack of 
dexterity are not welcome in the “tribe”. To mitigate this effect, it is recommended to 
implementation of a content humanization strategy (The Smiling Warrior). This 
involves creating an editorial line of videos (Reels/TikToks) and testimonials that 
show real beginners falling, laughing and learning in a safe environment accompanied by 
instructors. 
By visually normalizing the learning process, reinforcing that “everything 
warrior starts from scratch”, the perception of elitism is reduced and the school is validated with the 
amateur audience, particularly in the comments section.

3rd – The current website, excessively focused on Saoloto’s philosophy and symbolism, 
does not answer the practical doubts and critical insecurities of those who have never had contact with the 
surfing (fear of the sea, technical difficulties, equipment, safety), leading to abandonment in 
moment of decision. It is recommended to develop a Landing Page dedicated to 
beginners (Zero-Friction Page), which replaces abstraction with clarity. 
This page should deconstruct the experience step by step (“What will you learn in 
your 1st class”), explicitly ensure that safety and equipment are included and 
use reassuring language. The objective is for it to function as a “safe haven” 
within the site, converting curiosity (high BSV) into trust and effective booking (CVR). 
A/B Testing 
As one of the services, aimed at the Portuguese market, is a 
class subscription, the A/B test variable will be the price presentation format. 
Regardless of whether the user selects a 3, 6 or 12 month package, the possibility 
test is whether the monetary value of the service should be shown as a monthly fee or as 
single payment. 
The central metric will be the number of clicks on the chosen preference, allowing 
identify which of the two presentations generates greater traction. The objective is to understand which 
format that the public values most and, based on that, automatically adopt the option with 
better CTR, reducing the number of clicks needed to convert. 
In summary, the 360º knowledge that the team has about the 
project. Although this is a fictitious exercise, the 
main issues inherent to the pre-launch, launch and post-launch phases, having

3. Conclusion 
The development of this project, focused on the creation and go-to-market strategy 
of Saoloto Surf School, allowed us to follow a complex itinerary that transformed a 
initial idea into a tangible, differentiated and operationally viable business model. Ao 
Throughout the various stages of this Business Case, we sought not only to structure a school of 
surfing, but building a brand with soul, capable of responding to the challenges of a market 
saturated through a unique value proposition: the fusion between Samoan spiritual heritage and 
the hospitality of Costa da Caparica. 
The initial phase of strategic diagnosis proved to be fundamental to support all 
subsequent decisions. The application of the 4C’s framework allowed us to deconstruct the scenario 
current competitive environment, where a clear saturation of the offer focused on performance was identified 
technology and mass tourism. The validation of Costa da Caparica as a physical location, 
to the detriment of Cascais, it was not just a geographical choice, but a decision to 
positioning: authenticity, wild nature and space for 
grow, moving the brand away from congested urban centers where the surfing "vibe" is lost 
in excessive commercialization. This analysis confirmed that although there are 678 schools 
surfing in Portugal, there is a blue ocean for anyone who sets out to sell not just lessons, 
but belonging. 
The construction of the brand identity, materialized in the Brand Guidelines, was the 
turning point that allowed Saoloto to stop being a theoretical project and come to life 
own. The definition of the name "Saoloto" (Freedom) and the motto "Where the Waves Carve 
Family" served as a compass for all tactical choices. As we focus on branding 
human and community, we respond directly to the pain identified in our 
personas.  
For Lukas, the experienced traveler, we offer the cultural depth that is missing in 
commercial schools; For Kelly, the independent woman, we guarantee safety and security 
welcoming a non-intimidating environment; and for Duarte, the local young man, we created a 
space of formation and identity. This psychographic segmentation, more than demographic, 
ensures that Saoloto communicates with emotional relevance, a critical factor in converting 
interest in loyalty in a market where the barrier to entry for the consumer is, many times, 
Sometimes, the fear of not belonging.

The Marketing Mix strategy (7Ps) and the communication ecosystem (POEM) 
demonstrated the ability to operationalize this philosophical vision. The decision to adopt a 
Competitive Pricing strategy in the Upper-Middle segment, supported by a strong 
digital presence and partnerships with influencers such as Teresa Bonvalot and Hunter Jones, 
positions Saoloto as an affordable premium offering. 
We don't sell the lowest price, we sell the highest perceived value: the down payment 
in a tribe. The structure of the ecosystem, from the top of the funnel with lifestyle content and 
storytelling (like the "Big Z" narrative) to conversion via Google Ads and Website 
optimized, proves that the brand is prepared to capture, nurture and convert leads in a 
efficient. The focus on video (Reels) and social proof (UGC) reflects an understanding 
deep understanding of the consumption habits of the Millennial and Gen Z generations, ensuring that the brand 
keeps it relevant and visible where consumer attention currently resides. 
From a feasibility and management point of view, the plan presented is realistic and 
conservative. The Build-Up budget strategy, focused on the essentials for the start-up, combined with 
to a rigorous control panel (Dashboard), allows constant monitoring of health 
of the business. 
Defining clear SMART objectives, from initial awareness to conversion rate 
retention in Surf Camps, guarantees that management will not be done by intuition, but by data. 
We are prepared to monitor Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Lifetime 
Value (LTV) from day one, allowing agile adjustments if the market reacts appropriately 
different than expected. 
Cross-strategies (SWOT) also demonstrated that Saoloto has 
planned resilience, with responses prepared for seasonality or 
aggressiveness of the competition, such as betting on packages for "Wave Poolers" or 
loyalty through quality of service. 
More than a business plan, this project presents a cultural manifesto. 
In an increasingly digital and isolated world, where surfing runs the risk of becoming just 
yet another fitness industry, Saoloto Surf School proposes a return to its origins. Proposes 
May the sea once again be a place of worship and connection. 
The conclusion we reached is that the viability of this project does not only lie in the 
quality of its waves or its boards, but in the strength of the community that aims to
